description: Use this when your client applies a written payment policy (AP2 vocabulary) and wants block, warn, log or allow with every reason; it is not a safety verdict, and we never block. One call before an agent pays: the payee facts, the agent's own context from our ledger (what it paid in the period, how often, whether and when it first paid this payee, how many new payees today), the out-of-character score of this payment as the agent's next, and a decision under a policy written in the AP2 mandate vocabulary (allowed_payees, amount_range, budget {max, period: daily|rolling_24h|rolling_7d}, agent_recurrence, execution_date) plus ours: new_payee {max, window_hours, max_new_per_day, step_up_ratio, step_up_days}, refuse_conditions {fact: block|warn|log|ignore} and signal {v2: {notable, major}}. Anything the evaluator does not understand fails closed. Named policies: log-only (default), balanced, recommended, recommended-v3, strict (their measured cost on 500 real agents is in the policy document). The answer is block / warn / log / allow with every reason, and is recorded (advisory since 1 Nov 2026; the default policy log-only never warns or blocks): we never block anything; your client decides, and decides its own fail mode when we are unreachable. Since 13 Nov 2026 every answer carries a receipt (gate.receipt.v2 since 24 Nov 2026): the agent, the payee, the amount, the policy by name and by the SHA-256 of all its limits, the decision, the reasons and the time, signed with Ed25519, to keep beside the payment as proof that it was checked first; receipts of checks made with a Desk session are also written into our signed log, which a daily Base transaction commits to (read one back at /api/gate/receipt?id=<decision_id>). A receipt never says a payment was made or that the payee is safe. Since 17 Nov 2026 (gate.context.v2) the context also counts what the Gate itself let through for the same caller in the last 12 hours and has not yet seen on chain, so a payment split into small parts meets the same limits: send the same client_ref with every check (a random string your client keeps outside the model's reach), or use a Desk session; a check with neither counts the ledger only and says so. Since 26 Nov 2026 the owner of an agent's registration can pin a policy to the agent (gate.policy.pin.v1): while a pin is in force the decision is the worse of the decision under the policy asked and the decision under the pinned policy, the answer adds pin, decision_asked, decision_pinned, decided_by and pin_reasons, and the receipt is gate.receipt.v3; asking with a weaker policy does not weaken the answer. Read an agent's pin at /api/gate/pin?agent=<registration number>.

agent.description: The paying agent: token id, act_8453_N, slug or bound wallet

client_ref.description: Optional: a random string of 16 to 64 characters (letters, digits, _ . -) that your client keeps and sends with every check; checks with the same client_ref count against each other until the ledger holds the payments

policy.description: Or your own policy object in the AP2 vocabulary; unknown keys fail closed

name: gate_check
title: Can this agent pay this address, now, this much? (free, advisory)
